scenarios.notes:
Line 283 was not reached. typeof WebGLRenderingContext and WebGL2RenderingContext stayed 'function' under these flags. three.js loaded, then the console showed 'THREE.WebGLRenderer: A WebGL context could not be created. Reason: disabled by enterprise policy or commandline switch' and 'Error creating WebGL context', and the catch at line 399 set the text.

The fallback was sent twice, reaching audio 43.8 s and 60.0 s after the DOM change. Chromium exposes the region as atomic (container-atomic:true, the implicit aria-atomic of role=status). For atomic regions Orca's liveregions._getMessage reads the container's current text when it processes each event. So the text-changed:insert event for 'Checking…', processed at 15:06:44.092 after the DOM already held the fallback, produced the fallback text, and the fallback's own insertion produced it a second time.

intended_first_load:
This is a proposed record, grounded in docs/site/geometry.mjs and museum.mjs at f61419d8 and in WAI-ARIA 1.2. role=status is a live region with an implicit aria-live=polite and an implicit aria-atomic=true. Content already in a region when the region appears is document content. Later changes to that region are announced politely, at the next graceful opportunity, without moving focus. Context for both widgets: museum.mjs appends the exhibit article to the already-loaded #active-exhibit only after the pinned sources verify (startMuseum, about lines 288-293). It then calls mountGeometry on a host that is already in the live document. Neither widget's status paragraph exists at page load; each is inserted dynamically, typically 0.5-1 s after navigation here. EC-014 (mountEC014): (a) The

is created with '2D coordinate diagram. Checking optional 3D view…' already set (line 273). It is appended in one task together with the hidden stage, the 2D figure and empty controls (line 279). So 'Checking…' is the initial content of a newly inserted region, not a change. It need not be announced, and it must be perceivable by reading. (b) The intended announcement on first load is the single later change of that same, already-present region: - success: the status3D text (lines 381 and 392), set after the awaited loadThree(); - library or WebGL creation failure: the line-399 text (catch); - later context loss: the line-375 text (webglcontextlost). Each is a status message under WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 and should be presented politely. (c) The line-283 branch (no WebGL globals) runs synchronously in the same task as the insertion. In that branch 'Checking…' is never exposed, and the fallback sentence is itself initial content of the inserted region: readable, but not required to be announced. (d) Each toggle activation (lines 382-389) is an intended polite announcement. It rewrites the region to either '2D coordinate diagram. All pin coordinates and six data labels remain visible.' or status3D. It also renames the focused button ('Show 3D view' / 'Show 2D diagram'), which the focused control exposes itself (4.1.2). P15 (drawP15): - The region is created empty (line 202) and appended with the figure and controls (line 240). redraw() fills it synchronously at line 242, in the same task. So 'Selected 3 of 3: the full triple is not two-decomposable.' is initial content of an inserted region: no announcement is required, and it must be readable. - Every later redraw() reassigns textContent. A changed sentence ('Selected 2 of 3: this proper subset is two-decomposable.' and back) is an intended polite status message. - Swap palette colors reassigns the identical sentence. No new information is conveyed and no announcement is required: the palette swap is visual only, and the SVG is role=img with a fixed aria-label. - Each toggle's own aria-pressed state belongs to the focused button (4.1.2), not to the live region. Applicable criteria: - SC 4.1.3 is met by the markup itself (role=status), whatever an AT chooses to do with content present at insertion. - Technique ARIA22, which needs the container present before the message, is met by the EC-014 async outcome, the toggles and context loss, and by the P15 later toggles. It is not applicable to either initial render. - Initial silence for EC-014 'Checking…', for the line-283 fallback or for the P15 initial fill is therefore not, by itself, a violation. - The same records stay distinct from C201-AT-01: the outer #museum-state, #conditional-route-status and .current-state lines are not covered here.
assessment_vs_intended:
Stack: Orca 46.1, Chromium 141.0.7390.37, AT-SPI 2.52, speech-dispatcher 0.12.0-rc2 with espeak-ng 1.51 into a real-time paced sink.

1. Initial content was spoken, which goes beyond what is required; there was no initial silence. Chromium fires object:text-changed:insert for the text of a newly inserted role=status paragraph, and Orca's live-region manager presents it.
- P15: the initial fill was spoken in every run (S4, S4X, S4F).
- EC-014: 'Checking optional 3D view…' was spoken only when Orca processed its insertion before the async outcome replaced it (S3, S3X). It was skipped in S1, S2, S5 and S3F. The region is atomic (Chromium container-atomic:true), and Orca builds the message from the container's current text when it processes each event. So a state replaced within about 0.05-0.6 s is skipped, and the final text can be duplicated (S2: fallback sent twice).
Neither outcome conflicts with the intended behaviour, under which announcing initial content is optional.

2. The intended async outcome was announced in every EC-014 run:
- library blocked (S1): line 399;
- WebGL disabled (S2): line 399, not line 283, because the WebGL globals remain defined;
- success (S3, S5, S3X, S3F): status3D;
- context loss (S5): line 375, audible about 0.6-0.8 s after the DOM change.

3. On first load the widget's outcome was audible only 44-73 s after the DOM change (S1-S5), or 31-53 s with the site's own #active-exhibit link form (S3F, S4F), where Orca skips Say All. Polite semantics permit queuing behind current speech, but this delay is not the widget's doing. In every run Orca queued, at the same MESSAGE priority and in FIFO order, 6-8 messages from the three outer status lines (C201-AT-01 scope) plus 2-3 Orca page-load messages, and the widget message waited behind them. With the default bare URL, Say All chunks were interleaved as well. This belongs to C201-AT-01 and is recorded here only as an observed interaction, not as a widget defect.

4. Later changes:
- EC-014 toggle rewrites were announced each time, 0.9 s (S3), about 0.1 s (S3F) and about 1.9 s after the key echo (S3X) after the DOM change.
- P15 toggle sentence changes were announced each time (S4: 0.9 s and 3.4 s; S4F: under 0.2 s; S4X: about 1.6 s). The focused toggle's aria-pressed change was announced when Orca's locus stayed on the button (S4F, and S4X on the second press).
- Swap palette colors produced no announcement in any run. Chromium fired children-changed remove and add with the identical text, and Orca sent nothing. This matches the intended 'no new information'.
- Renames of the focused EC-014 button were presented whenever Orca's locus was on the button (S3F, S3X step 5).

5. Deviations caused by the AT or the harness, not the widgets:
- With the prescribed CDP keys (S3, S4), Orca never sees the key press. Say All keeps running and moves Orca's locus of focus to its reading position, which suppresses rename and pressed-state speech for the focused control.
- With real X keys (S3X, S4X), Orca echoes 'return', cancels Say All, and on the first press moves DOM focus to its reading position (a link, or main). That is Orca Say All behaviour.

Overall: for both widgets the observed first-load and toggle speech matches or exceeds the intended behaviour. The material first-load finding is the 30-73 s queue delay behind the outer status lines, which is C201-AT-01 territory. The one unexercised path is line 283.
problems: The earlier r332adv harness never actually produced speech. Its Orca logs show 'Speech Dispatcher service failed to connect' (autospawn refused with 'already running') and 52 'Cannot get speech server' lines, so their SPEECH OUTPUT lines were never sent to a synthesizer. Fixed here: speech-dispatcher is started explicitly with a scratch config and SPEECHD_ADDRESS. All 9 runs show 0 'Cannot get speech server' lines and non-empty audio.raw files.

This Chromium does not trust the agent-proxy TLS CA. raw.githubusercontent.com fetches failed with ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID, and the first S3 attempt showed 'Unavailable…' with no exhibit. Worked around without disabling TLS: the driver relays the pinned sources through curl (which trusts the proxy CA) into evidence/raw_cache and serves them with CDP Fetch.fulfillRequest. The page still verified every byte count and SHA-256 itself; for example, the EC-014 source c5e64b9b… and the P15 source 87521901… match museum.json.

Nothing was listened to. espeak-ng audio goes through speech-dispatcher's ALSA output into a pipe consumed at real-time rate by scripts/audio_pacer.py, which saves audio.raw and burst times. 'Played' times come from the speech-dispatcher playback thread, which can lead actual sink consumption by up to the ALSA buffer: about 1.4 s for a 2.2 s utterance in S3F, with audio_pacer.log as ground truth. Pronunciation and audibility were not verified.

CDP Input.dispatchKeyEvent, which the task prescribes, is invisible to Orca: no key echo, no presentationInterrupt or CANCEL, and Say All on load keeps running. In S3 and S4 this suppressed Orca's presentation of the focused button's rename and pressed state, which a physical key press would not. The XTest variants S3X and S4X were added to show the difference. They use AT-SPI generate_keyboard_event, not the prescribed path.

S2 did not exercise geometry.mjs line 283. Under --disable-webgl --disable-3d-apis, typeof WebGLRenderingContext and WebGL2RenderingContext stay 'function', so the run reached the catch at line 399 instead. No run in Chromium 141 reached line 283, and I did not delete the globals artificially.

Orca's debug log is buffered and loses its last lines when Orca is stopped. Two messages per run at most were missing from it: one Say All chunk in S2 and the final widget status in S3F. extract.py recovers such messages from the speech-dispatcher log and marks them speechd-only. Raw orca-debug.txt files are kept unmodified with sha256 recorded.

The deployed Pages bytes could not be fetched. *.github.io is refused, the github-pages artifact download is refused (gh will not follow the blob-storage redirect), and the pages and pages/builds/latest API paths return 403. The identity claim is therefore limited to the git blobs of deployment 7314462071's commit. The deploy workflow regenerates docs/site before upload, so deployed museum.html probably differs in its CURRENT-SITE block.

Default Orca settings mean Say All on load for the bare ?view= URLs the task names. The site's own exhibit links use #active-exhibit, which suppresses Say All, so S3F and S4F were added. First-load timings depend on this choice and on load order: 'Page has … headings' varies between runs.

Whether 'Checking optional 3D view…' is spoken is a timing race between the async outcome and Orca's event processing: spoken in S3 and S3X, not in S1, S2, S5 and S3F. It cannot be treated as deterministic.
The two early S3 trial runs (one without the source relay, one with shorter waits) were overwritten by the final S3 run and are not retained as evidence. No claim in this report relies on them.

Pre-navigation setup: Chrome starts on a neutral data: page so that focus is in web content rather than the omnibox. Orca speaks that page ('c220 start…') before navigation; this is step 0 in each scenario.
